descriptors.concept_name: DEFECTS IN APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS NOT TO INVALIDATE ACTIONS TAKEN [SECTION 176]
descriptors.definition: Actions performed by a director remain fully valid and binding despite any subsequent discovery of appointment defects, disqualifications, or termination provisions. However, this protective validation ceases for any acts executed after the company officially notices the invalidity or termination of the appointment.
inclusion: Acts done before discovering appointment irregularities
Actions by managing or whole-time directors before general meeting disapproval
exclusion: Acts executed after the company notices appointment invalidity
Actions that are ultra vires the company or statute
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from acts performed post-notice of invalidity which receive no statutory validation

descriptors.definition: Companies are generally prohibited from directly or indirectly advancing loans, book debts, guarantees, or securities to their directors, relatives, partners, or associated firms. Specific relaxations permit such financial assistance only if approved via special resolution with detailed explanatory statements and utilized strictly for principal business activities.
terminology: Person in whom director is interested
inclusion: Direct and indirect loan advancements
Provision of guarantees or securities for loans taken by directors or connected entities
exclusion: Exempted transactions specifically provided under statutory non-applicability provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general inter-corporate loans under Section 186 due to targeted restrictions on key management personnel and related entities

descriptors.definition: Companies are restricted from making investments through more than two layers of investment companies to prevent the flagrant diversion of corporate funds. Specific exceptions apply when acquiring foreign companies with multi-layered investment subsidiaries or when maintaining mandatory legal subsidiaries.
inclusion: Acquisitions of shares, debentures, or other securities
Investments through permitted subsidiary layers
exclusion: Investments exceeding two layers outside the permitted statutory exceptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from director-specific loan prohibitions under Section 185 by focusing broadly on multi-layered corporate structures and quantitative investment limits

descriptors.concept_name: INVESTMENTS OF COMPANY TO BE HELD IN ITS OWN NAME [SECTION 187]
descriptors.definition: Companies must execute and maintain all investments in properties, securities, or assets strictly in their own corporate name. Specific statutory exemptions permit holding shares through nominees solely to maintain statutory membership limits or depositing assets with bankers and security holders under prescribed conditions.
inclusion: Investments held in subsidiary companies via nominees to satisfy statutory member minimums
Depositing securities with bankers for dividend collection or transfer facilitation
exclusion: Holding general corporate investments in unverified external names without a qualifying statutory exemption
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general investment authorization rules by strictly governing the legal title registration and custody mechanics of existing investments

descriptors.definition: Transactions between a company and its specified related parties—including directors, key managerial personnel, holding or subsidiary bodies, and associated entities—are stringently regulated. These frameworks require proper definitions of relational status to govern commercial dealings and corporate disclosures effectively.
instrument_references: Rule 15 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Relationships involving directors, KMPs, and their relatives
Corporate affiliations such as holding, subsidiary, and investing structures
exclusion: Professional advice, directions, or instructions given in a professional capacity
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general board contracts by establishing a precise legal threshold of connectedness that dictates special approval pathways

descriptors.concept_name: REGISTER OF CONTRACTS OR ARRANGEMENTS IN WHICH DIRECTORS ARE INTERESTED [SECTION 189]
descriptors.definition: Companies must mandatorily maintain a chronological register documenting particulars of all contracts and arrangements involving interested directors or related parties. These entries must be authenticated immediately, placed before the subsequent board meeting, and signed by all attending directors.
instrument_references: Rule 16 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Particulars of entities where directors hold concern or interest
Details of related party transactions governed by Section 188
exclusion: Holdings where a director together with others holds two percent or less of the paid-up share capital
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial director disclosures under Section 184 by acting as a consolidated statutory register maintained in a specific format

descriptors.concept_name: CONTRACT OF EMPLOYMENT WITH MANAGING OR WHOLE-TIME DIRECTORS [SECTION 190]
descriptors.definition: Companies must retain copies of written employment contracts or formal written memoranda detailing service terms for managing or whole-time directors at their registered office. These documents remain freely open to inspection by any company member without payment of fees, subject to specific penalties for non-compliance.
inclusion: Written service contracts with managing or whole-time directors
Written memoranda detailing unwritten service arrangements
exclusion: Private companies, which are statutorily exempted from these specific requirements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general board meeting minutes by specifically targeting executive service agreements and member inspection rights

descriptors.concept_name: PAYMENT TO DIRECTOR FOR LOSS OF OFFICE, ETC., IN CONNECTION WITH TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING, PROPERTY OR SHARES [SECTION 191]
descriptors.definition: Directors are prohibited from receiving compensation for loss of office or retirement during property, undertaking, or share transfers unless full particulars are disclosed and approved by members in a general meeting. This safeguards shareholders by ensuring transparency when control changes or company assets are transferred.
instrument_references: Rule 17 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Payments connected to the transfer of company undertakings or properties
Consideration resulting from general or conditional share transfer offers
exclusion: Payments made without prior member disclosure and general meeting approval
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard managerial remuneration by specifically governing compensatory exit payouts tied to corporate restructuring or asset transfers

descriptors.concept_name: RESTRICTION ON NON-CASH TRANSACTIONS INVOLVING DIRECTORS [SECTION 192]
descriptors.definition: Companies and their holding, subsidiary, or associate entities are prohibited from entering into non-cash asset acquisition arrangements with directors or connected persons without prior approval via a general meeting resolution. Valuations for these transactions must be established by a registered valuer and included in the meeting notice.
inclusion: Asset acquisitions for considerations other than cash involving directors or connected persons
Arrangements requiring valuations by registered valuers
exclusion: Transactions where restitution is impossible and indemnification applies, or bona fide value acquisitions without notice
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from monetary loans and related party contracts by specifically targeting non-cash asset swaps between companies and directors

descriptors.definition: When a One Person Company enters into a contract with its sole member who also serves as its director, the terms must be recorded in writing, in a memorandum, or in the subsequent board meeting minutes. Ordinary course business contracts are exempt, while recorded contracts must be reported to the Registrar within fifteen days.
inclusion: Non-standard contracts between an OPC and its sole member-director
Recording contract terms in board meeting minutes
exclusion: Contracts executed in the ordinary course of business
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from multi-member corporate contracts by addressing the unique governance risks of single-member control structures
